subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on a node host connected to a non-loopback gateway fail closed before OAuth starts, or should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned credential forwarding path?
rationale: Both repairs decide where OAuth refresh credentials are minted and stored, so automation should not choose the cross-host credential policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
options.body: Block the login before OAuth/token creation when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to authenticate on the gateway host.

options.title: Design Gateway Credential Sync
options.body: Keep node-host auth convenience by adding an explicit gateway credential-transfer API with security review, tests, and operator-visible behavior.

options.title: Document Node-Local Auth Only
options.body: Keep current storage behavior but clearly warn that node-host auth login does not update the gateway credential store.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
recommendation.body: Block the login before OAuth/token creation when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to authenticate on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current signal from recent auth history and the prior maintainer remote-node OAuth guard attempt.
